preconditions.description: The number of test cases t is an integer between 1 and 10^4 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(n.is_integer() and 2 <= n <= 2*10**5 for n in [int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2]])
preconditions.description: Each test case has an integer n (number of vertices) between 2 and 2*10^5 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(len(a) == n and all(1 <= ai <= 10**6 for ai in a) for n, a in zip([int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2]], [list(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::2]]))
preconditions.description: Each test case has n integers a_i (altitudes) between 1 and 10^6 inclusive.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly t lines, one for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(output_line.is_integer() and 0 <= int(output_line) <= n*(n-1)//2 for output_line, n in zip(stdout.splitlines(), [int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2]]))
postconditions.description: Each output line is an integer representing the maximum possible number of edges for the corresponding test case, between 0 and n*(n-1)//2 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: all(edges <= n*(n-1)//2 for edges, n in zip([int(line) for line in stdout.splitlines()], [int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2]]))
postconditions.description: The output edges for each test case do not exceed the theoretical maximum possible edges in a simple graph (n*(n-1)//2).

postconditions.expression: all(edges == max_possible_edges(a) for edges, a in zip([int(line) for line in stdout.splitlines()], [list(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::2]]))
postconditions.description: The output edges for each test case is the maximum possible number of edges in a graph with n vertices and altitudes a_i, such that there are no three distinct vertices u, v, w with a_u ≤ a_v ≤ a_w and edges (u,v) and (v,w) existing.
